$comment: Fixtures for stripCarrierUnicode (detect_ai_tells.ts). Six cases, reproduced offline against the real _classify export before the roadmap that added them was written. Escapes are JSON \u forms so the file is reviewable in a diff: a fixture whose payload is invisible in review is a fixture nobody can check.

recorded_limitation.what: The complex-script preservation cases are a CURATED BLOCK SET, not a Unicode Script-property lookup.
tested_blocks: emoji ZWJ sequences (U+1F400-U+1FAFF joined by U+200D)
recorded_limitation.untested: Indic (Devanagari, Bengali, Tamil, ...), Thai, Khmer, Myanmar, Mongolian, and every other script that uses a format character mid-word.
recorded_limitation.why_this_is_acceptable: The predicate errs toward PRESERVATION: a carrier is removed only when both neighbours are ASCII, so a format character inside a non-ASCII word is preserved whatever its script. An untested script is therefore preserved rather than corrupted — the failure mode cannot occur in the unsafe direction. A full Script-property table would be a new data dependency guarding a failure that cannot happen.
recorded_limitation.what_would_change_this: A script whose format characters legitimately appear between two ASCII characters. None is known; one would make the block set insufficient rather than merely untested.

cases.name: clean prose is a no-op, and the strip is idempotent
cases.input: Nothing hidden here — just prose with an em dash.
cases.expect_out: Nothing hidden here — just prose with an em dash.
